Trustworthy guidance

Keep expectations high. Make participation possible.

Language support should open access to grade-level thinking—not quietly replace it. Start with learner strengths, offer more than one way to make meaning, and adjust support using evidence from the lesson.

Plan with a colleague
01

Home language is an asset

Use all available language resources to build meaning, connection, and confidence.

02

Support the language, not less thinking

Keep the learning goal visible while changing how students access and express it.

03

Notice, then fade

Remove a scaffold when evidence shows the learner can take the next step independently.

Prototype note Assessment accommodations and school policies should be approved locally and labelled separately from classroom practice.

Make co-planning easier
